items.text: WTI down 4.7% and Brent down 5.2% week-on-week (as of Nov 11), easing near-term inflation pressure but signaling demand concerns. Oil's weakness reflects both a softer China PMI (49.3 in Oct, in contraction) and ECB-on-hold bias—marginal relief for high-yield spreads, though energy volatility remains a tail risk for special situations in both energetics and working-capital-sensitive sectors.

Jobless claims rising to 200k (vs 191k prior, as of Nov 7) amid 165k October payroll beat, creating mixed signals—headline strength masking potential softness below. Unemployment held at 4.1%, wage growth ticking at 3.12% YoY. For credit, gradual labor loosening is credit-negative but predictable; watch next two months for acceleration that could trigger wider spread repricing.

Headline CPI at 3.72% and core at 2.57% (Sep data, most recent), with PPI upticking to 6.52% (Oct), pointing to stubborn input costs despite energy relief. PCE core remains elevated at 3.12% YoY. Sticky inflation keeps Fed neutral and 10Y yields firm at 5.12%, pressuring leveraged credit financing and extending refinance uncertainty—a material headwind for stressed issuers and distressed M&A.

Fed funds unchanged at 4.0%, 2Y/10Y curve inversion easing to 29bp (vs 25bp prior), and ECB deposit rate locked at 2.50% with 94% market odds of a December hike. Policy divergence (Fed hold vs ECB tightening) supports longer duration but curbs refinance relief; terminal rate expectations haven't fallen, leaving distressed names with muted refi windows and high rollover risk.

HY OAS at 334bp (up 4bp), IG OAS at 90bp (flat), CCC OAS at 1,310bp (down 20bp, slight relief). Modest tightening in CCC suggests some appetite for deeply distressed names, but macro uncertainty (VIX +298bp to 22.91 from 19.92) remains elevated. Special situations investors should view recent CCC tightness as window, not trend, given refinance walls and earnings recession risk ahead.

GDPnow at 3.38% (tracking fast), but retail sales ex-autos only +0.2% m/m in Oct and retail YoY growth at 8.14% (Oct data). University of Michigan sentiment recovered to 51 (Nov prelim, well above 48 Oct), but remains historically depressed; personal saving rate fell to 3.8% (Sep), signaling limited consumer cushion. Housing starts and existing home sales both declining (1.22M and 3.75M SAAR, Oct data). Bifurcated growth narrative—GDP momentum vs. household stress—creates opportunity for selective credit dislocations.

30-year mortgage rate at 7.11% (Nov 12), up from 7.18%, holding near cycle peaks; existing home sales down 5.6% YoY and housing starts down 5.2% YoY (Sep data, most recent). Builder spreads likely under pressure and mortgage-dependent credit (MBS pools, servicer bonds, home-equity lenders) faces duration risk and negative carry. Risk window: if rates stabilize near 5% 10Y, housing could stabilize, triggering mean reversion in distressed mortgage-credit; monitor next CPI for refi signals.

themeCards.title: Energy Shock & Credit Spillover
themeCards.statusLine: Oil down sharply from $94–$98 in early Nov to $89.62 WTI; ECB cited energy shock as uncertainty driver. Demand-driven weakness (not supply) suggests demand destruction in both EM and core.
themeCards.relevance: Energy-linked credits (renewables JV debt, energy infrastructure MLPs, E&P balance sheets) face margin compression; special situations investors should screen for unhedged commodity exposure and working-capital strains in mid-cap energy supply chains.

themeCards.title: China Demand Collapse
themeCards.statusLine: Official NBS PMI at 49.3 (Oct), new orders at 49.4, exports at 48.7—broadbased contraction despite high-tech resilience. SME PMI at 47.5, suggesting demand destruction below large-cap veneer.
themeCards.relevance: Spillover to US industrial credit: auto suppliers, chemical/materials exporters, and industrial equipment OEMs face FX headwinds and volume derating; European & Asian credit markets pricing contagion—dollar strength and China credit tightness create refinance windows for distressed US corporates.

themeCards.title: Mortgage Refinance Wall (2027–28)
themeCards.statusLine: 10Y at 5.12% and 30-year mortgage at 7.11%; housing starts and existing sales both declining; refinance activity nearly frozen. Wave of balloons and rate resets in 2027–28 housing book will pressure household credit quality.
themeCards.relevance: Direct impact: mortgage servicer spreads, MBS-backed bonds, and home-equity lender credit (mortgage REITs, captive finance arms) face duration compression and roll-down risk; indirect: consumer default spillover into auto loans, credit cards, and retail PMD books by late 2027.

themeCards.title: Sticky Core Inflation & Rate Terminal
themeCards.statusLine: Core CPI 2.57% (Sep), core PCE 3.12% (Sep), PPI 6.52% (Oct) all sticky; Fed on pause, ECB may hike Dec; terminal rate expectations have not fallen materially despite energy decline.
themeCards.relevance: Refinance relief is off the table for 2027; leveraged-credit issuers face elevated debt-service costs; default probabilities rising in BB-to-CCC space; rising-rate credit (floating-rate exposure in bank debt, CLOs) benefits, but equity downside on earnings misses will pressure subordinated structures and high-yield mezzanine.

themeCards.title: Labor Softening Inflection Risk
themeCards.statusLine: Jobless claims popped to 200k (vs 191k prior); unemployment 4.1%, wage growth 3.12% YoY. Payrolls still strong at +165k (Oct) but starting from softer base; next two months are critical for momentum signal.
themeCards.relevance: Early-warning system for mid-2027 earnings disappointments and consumer default acceleration. Credit investors should use 6-week window (now through year-end) to rotate out of consumer-discretionary and labor-intensive credits (retail, QSR, apparel) before labor data confirms rolling recession.

themeCards.title: Sentiment Rebound vs. Structural Household Stress
themeCards.statusLine: UMich sentiment jumped to 51.0 (Nov prelim, beat 48.0 consensus), but personal saving rate fell to 3.8% (Sep); existing home sales off -5.6% YoY. Sentiment gain was pre-election, before post-election volatility.
themeCards.relevance: Sentiment bounce is fragile; household savings buffer eroding, mortgage stress rising, durable goods orders likely to disappoint. For credit: consumer-staples and consumer-discretionary PM will face margin pressure from both sticky costs (via pricing power erosion) and demand destruction (via unemployment acceleration); watch for covenant waivers and covenant loosening requests in Q4 earnings calls.

regime.label: Late-cycle friction
regime.detail: Rates terminal, inflation sticky, labor softening, credit costs high, refinance frozen, China weak, sentiment fragile—high-yield spreads modest despite tail risks; default risk rising in BB–CCC; special situations window narrowing.
